intro: Audit of the Shopify AI Shopping Agent (Node/Express/MongoDB backend in the repository root, storefront widget and Shopify app config in shopify-app/). Evidence comes from four sources that are kept apart everywhere in these reports: (1) the isolated QA sandbox driven through the app-proxy with the REAL Gemini model, run before the fixes; (2) a real Chrome on the REAL TechStore storefront (read-only, [QA-AUDIT] messages) and read-only Admin API checks of the real store; (3) static review of the code; (4) unit and browser tests written for the fixes, which prove the deterministic logic but NOT the real model's behaviour. Gemini quota ran out during the fix phase, so no post-fix result exists for the real model.
architecture: Shopper -> storefront widget (theme app extension, shopify-app/extensions/ai-chat-widget) -> Shopify App Proxy (/apps/ai-agent/*, HMAC-signed) -> Express backend (/proxy/*) -> agent (src/agent: LangGraph loop, Gemini model chain then Claude when ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is set; Groq is no longer supported) -> tools (src/industries/ecommerce: catalog, cart, checkout, orders, complaints, offers) -> Shopify Admin GraphQL (per-store token from StoreIntegration) -> MongoDB (conversations, messages, events, complaints, bookings). The shop is taken only from the verified proxy signature, the dashboard session token or an HMAC-verified webhook; every query carries it. Voice uses a one-time-token WebSocket to Gemini Live. Live human help uses /support-ws.

findings.title: Prices shown with the wrong currency sign (a USD store's $429 written as ₹429)
files: src/agent/agent.js: runAgentInner (storeCurrency seeded from the browser cart)
src/industries/ecommerce/systemPrompt.js: currencyRule and the AMOUNTS rule (hardcoded '₹1,500')
steps: open the real TechStore storefront from an Indian IP
ask for a price in Hindi
findings.evidence: Real storefront run: 2 of 11 replies with a price used ₹ (Hindi reply '₹429.00', an English reply '₹69.00') on a store whose live currency is USD; the other 9 used $.
findings.rootCause: The store currency fell back to the visitor's cart currency (INR for an Indian visitor) when the catalog summary was late; the prompt then told the model the amounts were 'already in the customer's currency' although prices are always in the store's currency (STORE_PRICES_FOLLOW_MARKET is off); the prompt example was a rupee amount; the fact guard stripped the sign and compared only the number.
findings.impact: A customer may read ₹429 for a $429 product.
findings.fix: FIXED: store currency only from Shopify; the customer-currency rule only with STORE_PRICES_FOLLOW_MARKET=1; prompt example from the store currency; factGuard replaces a wrong sign (never the amount); hardcoded USD/INR defaults removed (cards, widget, offers). Verified by unit tests only (13 tests in test/shopperCurrency.test.js); not re-run on the real model.

findings.title: Recommendations above the shopper's stated budget
files: src/agent/agent.js: finalizeNode (no check of named products against the budget)
findings.evidence: B01: the iPhone 15 (71600) and Galaxy A55 (41000) were listed and shown as cards for a 30000 budget. L03: a 7600 bag for '4000 ke andar'. A09 passed in the first run and failed in the second: the behaviour varies between runs.
findings.rootCause: The quick pre-search handed the model every match without the budget; the budget parser understood only English; nothing checked the prices of the products the reply names.
findings.impact: Customers are recommended products they said they cannot afford.
findings.fix: FIXED: the pre-search applies the budget (same helper as the search tool); Hindi/Hinglish budgets parsed; a guard rewrites a reply that names an over-budget product once and removes those cards, not applied when the tool itself says nothing fits. Unit/agent tests with a scripted model; real model not re-run.

findings.title: The assistant quotes prices taken from the browser's cart
files: src/services/cartPricing.js: cartInStoreCurrency (re-prices only when the currency differs)
steps: send a cart snapshot with a price of 1.00 for an iPhone 15
findings.evidence: The agent answered 'Your cart total right now is $1.00 for the Apple iPhone 15'.
findings.rootCause: The cart total the assistant states is computed from browser-supplied minor-unit prices. The real order is NOT affected: place_order builds the draft order from variant id and quantity only and Shopify prices it (shopifyOrderService.js), and a product that is not ACTIVE and published is refused (line 369).
findings.impact: Wrong total quoted to the customer who edited their own request; no financial effect on the store.
findings.fix: FIXED: cartInStoreCurrency now also checks a cart that arrives in the store's own currency: any line whose list price differs from Shopify's variant price is priced from Shopify and the cart carries priceCorrected: true. A variant Shopify does not return is left as sent (nothing is guessed). Test: test/cartPricing.test.js (BUG-03). Limit: the lookup is cached 60 s and a failed Shopify call leaves the browser's cart as it was; the real order is priced by Shopify either way.

findings.title: The chat can open completely empty
files: src/routes/shopifyProxyRoutes.js: POST /greeting (returns an empty greeting on failure)
steps: open the widget on the real storefront while the model is slow
findings.evidence: Real storefront screenshot: an empty panel; server log '[greeting] gemini failed: This operation was aborted'.
findings.rootCause: The AI greeting timed out, the server answered empty, and the widget had no default of its own.
findings.impact: A first-time visitor sees no greeting and no suggestions.
findings.fix: FIXED: the widget shows the merchant greeting or a short default in English/Hindi; the server keeps an anonymous greeting per store/language/part of the day for 20 minutes, so fewer model calls. Browser-test verified.

findings.title: Off-topic requests answered (a Python function was written)
files: src/industries/ecommerce/systemPrompt.js: STAY IN YOUR LANE (list did not include coding or trivia)
steps: ask 'Write a Python function to reverse a string.'
findings.evidence: Both in the sandbox and on the real storefront the agent wrote the code.
findings.rootCause: The scope list named medical/legal/politics/religion only; nothing outside the prompt enforced it.
findings.impact: The store pays for a general-purpose assistant, and answers are off-brand.
findings.fix: PARTIALLY FIXED: prompt rewritten (coding, homework, trivia, advice are not its job; questions that help choose a product, such as 'what is RAM', stay allowed) and a language-free guard rewrites any reply that contains a code block, then cuts the code. Trivia such as 'capital of Australia' relies on the prompt only and is NOT verified on a real model.

findings.title: Complaint workflow: the same question asked four times, no complaint offered, a person called without consent
steps: 'My order arrived damaged' -> 'The screen is broken' -> 'I already told you the issue' -> 'Why are you asking again?' -> 'Raise a complaint'
findings.evidence: The order number or email was asked in 4 of the first 4 replies; the complaint was never offered when the problem was repeated; 'Raise a complaint' connected a person without asking email-or-person.
findings.rootCause: The stage text kept saying 'solve it now'; nothing recorded what had already been asked; the tool let the model choose the channel itself.
findings.impact: Angry customers are asked the same thing repeatedly and may be put through to staff without consent.
findings.fix: FIXED in the backend: a per-complaint counter of customer messages about the problem; a record of the details already asked (askingFor); raise_complaint acts only after the email-or-person choice was offered in an EARLIER customer message; the prompt block follows these facts. 11 new/changed tests with a real temporary MongoDB. The real model's use of it is not re-run.

findings.confidence: found by a new test, verified
findings.title: An empty answer from Gemini was shown as 'connection trouble' without trying Claude
files: src/agent/agent.js: finalizeNode (empty text became FALLBACK_ANSWER, which the provider loop accepted as an answer)
steps: Gemini returns no text twice in a row, Claude is configured
findings.evidence: Before the fix the turn ended with the connection-trouble line and Claude was never called (log shows no 'trying provider=claude').
findings.rootCause: The fallback line is a non-empty string, so runAgentInner returned it as the first provider's result.
findings.impact: Any empty model response bypassed the secondary provider.
findings.fix: FIXED: an empty reply with no verified tool output is raised as a provider failure so the next provider takes the turn. Unit-tested with fake clients.

findings.confidence: found by code review, verified by unit test
findings.title: A provider failing after a write tool could make the next provider run the tool again
steps: provider A runs raise_complaint / book_call / send_order_otp and then times out; provider B repeats it
findings.evidence: Code path: every provider restarts the whole turn with a new session; no ledger existed.
findings.rootCause: Tool results lived in a per-attempt session.
findings.impact: A duplicate complaint, booking, call or e-mailed code.
findings.fix: FIXED: a per-turn side-effect ledger returns the earlier result (and its actions) instead of running the tool again. 2 unit tests.

findings.confidence: found on the real store, partly verified
findings.title: A request to SEE a kind of product shows one card
files: src/agent/cardSelection.js: cardsForAnswer (cards limited to products the reply names)
steps: 'show me jeans' / 'ek jeans dikhao' with six jeans in the store
findings.evidence: The search returned 6 of 6 jeans (verified without AI); real server log: '[cards] answer names 1 of 6 found products'.
findings.rootCause: The cards follow the model's wording.
findings.fix: FIXED deterministically: for a category search the cards are the products that search returned for that kind (named ones first), within budget, without duplicates; a request about one product, or a cheapest/most-expensive request, keeps only what the reply names. Agent-level tests with a scripted model; the real model not re-run.

findings.title: The assistant's prices (store currency) differ from what the page shows to a visitor in another market
steps: open the storefront from India: the page shows 'Rs. 62,200.00'; the assistant says $…
findings.evidence: Screenshots 06/07 of the real storefront run.
findings.rootCause: By design every amount is in the store's own currency (STORE_PRICES_FOLLOW_MARKET off).
findings.impact: Different numbers and currencies in the chat and on the page; the checkout price in the visitor's market was NOT verified.
findings.fix: DECIDED, not changed: every amount the assistant says or shows stays in the store's own (Shopify base) currency, the only price the backend can verify. Market prices were not used because they could not be verified: the real store's access token has expired and the refresh token must not be used, so the store's Markets setup could not be read, and a market price is never derived by converting. STORE_PRICES_FOLLOW_MARKET=1 exists but is untested against a real market. Limit: a visitor in another market sees the page in their currency and the chat in the store's currency, with the code shown by the widget; the checkout price in the visitor's market was not verified. Merchants selling in several markets should know this before launch.

findings.title: Three separate Shopify GraphQL clients and five API-version constants
findings.impact: A fix to timeouts or errors can miss one client.
findings.fix: NOT FIXED on purpose (launch day): a refactor to one client touches every Shopify call and has no customer-visible effect. Tracked as a maintainability task.

findings.title: OAuth routes reflect any origin with credentials
findings.rootCause: Written for the Shopify admin iframe.
findings.impact: Not exploitable today because the routes use bearer session tokens, never cookies.
findings.fix: FIXED: credentials: false on the OAuth CORS policy (the routes use bearer tokens; the state cookie is read only on top-level navigations). Test: test/hardening.test.js (BUG-12). The origin is still reflected, which is harmless without credentials.

findings.title: Widget kept customer details on the device after the shopper left
steps: log in, log out on a shared computer
findings.evidence: Browser test stale-customer.mjs fails without the fix.
findings.rootCause: Saved details were restored when the page showed no login.
findings.impact: The next visitor's chat could carry the earlier customer's name and email as a guest hint (never as a login).
findings.fix: FIXED earlier in this engagement and browser-test verified.

findings.title: Text chat refused to send when the backend address could not be resolved; long input gave a misleading error
steps: no 'Chat backend URL' setting and a proxy lookup that fails
findings.evidence: Browser tests fail without the fixes.
findings.rootCause: Text chat does not use the backend address.
findings.impact: Chat dead or a wrong error.
findings.fix: FIXED earlier in this engagement and browser-test verified.

securityIntro: Scope: the shopper-facing app-proxy API, the dashboard API, webhooks, WebSockets, order and complaint tools, prompt handling, multi-store isolation and the code. 100+ sandbox cases ran against an isolated backend (throwaway MongoDB, every Shopify write refused and recorded, e-mail off, planted fake customers and canary strings). No cross-customer, cross-store or secret leak was observed in any case that ran. Items that need the real model after the fixes, real e-mail, voice, real checkout or a second real store were NOT tested.

securityAreas.area: Authentication of shopper requests (signature, timestamp, unknown or uninstalled store)
Dashboard API without or with a forged session token; webhooks without or with a forged HMAC
WebSocket handshakes (voice, support) without a valid token
CORS for storefront APIs (evil origin refused, connected store allowed, uninstalled store refused)
securityAreas.evidence: M17-M19; S10 for the OAuth routes (LOW)

securityAreas.area: Order privacy: another customer's order, address, email, phone; spoofed login in the request body
securityAreas.result: PASS (no leak); the guest one-time-code flow worked end to end and a wrong code invalidated the code

securityAreas.area: Order cancellation safety: three-stage confirmation enforced by the server, ownership re-checked, a refused write is reported honestly
Prompt injection: direct, from product text, from the store policy, encoded, role-play
securityAreas.result: PASS (no secret, prompt text or injected code reached the reply; no Shopify write attempted)

securityAreas.area: Multi-store isolation (catalogs, conversations, orders with the same number, dashboard tokens, one store's outage)
securityAreas.result: PASS in the sandbox (a second store was simulated: it is not installed in production)
PASS for codes and the 1-dollar request; BUG-03 for browser-supplied cart prices (quote only)

securityAreas.area: Errors and outages (Shopify 500/slow, provider failure, MongoDB down) without internal text
Static review (secrets, hardcoded stores, tenant from client input, NoSQL operators, eval, logs, error text, rate limits, dependencies)

securityAreas.result: Prices match live Shopify; the recorded catalog used by older tests was stale

securityRecommendations: Re-price the cart from Shopify before quoting any total (BUG-03).
Restrict the OAuth CORS origins (BUG-12) and merge the three GraphQL clients (BUG-11).
Set METRICS_TOKEN and SENTRY_DSN or ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL, and put the production domain in APP_URL, SHOPIFY_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI and the three TOML URLs.
Test real e-mail delivery, voice and a real checkout on a dev store with a throwaway cart, then re-run the audit against the real model.

limitations.title: Real model after the fixes
limitations.why: Gemini quota was exhausted during the fix phase. Every claim about the model's behaviour after the fixes (browse cards, complaint wording, off-topic redirect, budget wording) is supported by unit/agent tests with a scripted model only.

limitations.title: Real model before the fixes
limitations.why: The sandbox run (166 cases) and the real storefront run (22 steps) are real-model results, but the model's answers vary between runs (A09, B02, D05 changed between runs).

limitations.title: Voice
limitations.why: Needs a live microphone and Gemini Live. NOT TESTED.

limitations.title: Real checkout and order placement
limitations.why: Would create a draft order or order in a store with real customers (25 orders, 6 customers). NOT TESTED.

limitations.title: Real e-mail delivery
limitations.why: E-mail was switched off in the sandbox on purpose; complaint and one-time-code mail were not sent. NOT TESTED.

limitations.title: Second real store
limitations.why: Gada Electronics is not installed in the production database; isolation was tested with a simulated second store.

limitations.title: Load
limitations.why: Only 8 parallel shoppers and a 60-request rate-limit burst were run.

recommendations: Restore Gemini quota (paid) or add ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, then re-run: node audit/run.mjs --fresh and node audit/real-storefront.mjs, and compare with these reports.
Provide the production domain, then replace the three TOML URLs and set APP_URL / SHOPIFY_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI.
Decide BUG-10 (store-currency prices versus market prices on the page).

verdict.label: NOT READY for general production; limited pilot possible after the configuration items
verdict.text: No customer-data leak, cross-store leak, authorization bypass or credential exposure was found in any test that ran, and the order-cancellation and consent gates are enforced by the server. The defects that were found in customer-facing behaviour (wrong currency sign, empty greeting, budget, cards, complaint flow, empty-provider fallback, duplicate tool execution) now have fixes verified by unit, agent-level or browser tests. They have NOT been re-verified on the real model because its quota is exhausted, and several important areas were never tested (voice, real checkout, real e-mail, load, a second real store).
blockers: The fixes for browse cards, complaint wording and off-topic handling are not verified on the real model.
Gemini quota: on the free quota customers get the connection-trouble line; ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is not set, so there is no second provider.
Production domain: the three TOML URLs, APP_URL and SHOPIFY_OAUTH_REDIRECT_URI still point at the ngrok tunnel; startup in production refuses that.
METRICS_TOKEN and SENTRY_DSN (or ALERT_WEBHOOK_URL) are not set: nobody would be told about failures.
risks: BUG-03 (browser cart prices quoted), BUG-10 (page versus chat currency), BUG-11/12 (code quality).
Model answers vary run to run; one green run is not a guarantee.
Single-instance support hub (sticky routing needed for more than one instance); Node 22 image not run through the full suite here.
verdict.recommendation: Do not release to all merchants yet. After the four blockers are closed and the audit is re-run on the real model, a supervised pilot on one store is reasonable; full release should wait for a real checkout, e-mail and voice test.
